study.title: Functional Recovery After Routine Knee Arthroplasty
study.background: Previous cohorts described walking function for 12 months after knee arthroplasty. Recovery during routine rehabilitation needs further characterization.
study.hypothesis: Observed outcomes may change during routine care; this observational study does not establish treatment superiority.

population.study_population: Adults undergoing routine rehabilitation after knee arthroplasty.
inclusion_criteria: Adults undergoing routine rehabilitation after knee arthroplasty.
exclusion_criteria: Records or planned follow-up information unavailable.

design.study_design: Ambispective, single-center observational cohort study of routine care.

arms.name: Routine care cohort
arms.description: Adults undergoing routine rehabilitation after knee arthroplasty.

design.intervention_name: Walking function and rehabilitation burden questionnaires

assessments: Walking function and rehabilitation burden questionnaires
procedures.discontinuation: Participants may withdraw at any time.

procedures: Walking function and rehabilitation burden questionnaires
Walking function and rehabilitation burden questionnaires
Walking function and rehabilitation burden questionnaires

safety.roles: The investigator assesses and reports safety events.

risks_benefits.risks: Questionnaires may cause inconvenience and record review creates confidentiality risks.
risks_benefits.injury_handling: Research-related concerns will be reported to the investigator.

statistics.analysis_plan: Continuous scores will be summarized using medians and interquartile ranges. Categorical outcomes will be summarized using counts and percentages. No hypothesis tests are planned.

objectives.primary: Assess the primary endpoint of walking function after knee arthroplasty.

introduction.text: Previous cohorts described walking function for one year after knee arthroplasty. Recovery during routine rehabilitation needs further characterization.

objectives.text: Evaluate the primary endpoint of walking function after knee replacement.

analysis-plan.methodology.text: Summarize numeric outcomes with the median and interquartile range, and categorical outcomes with frequencies and proportions. The analysis remains descriptive without hypothesis testing.

icf.procedures.text: Study assessments involve walking function and rehabilitation burden questionnaires at Baseline on Day 0, Month 1 on Day 30 with a seven day window, and Month 3 on Day 90 with a seven day window. Eligible adults are 18 to 80 years old. Adults undergoing routine rehabilitation after knee arthroplasty. Records or planned follow-up information must be available. You must not have taken part in another study during the ninety days before screening.

prs_objective: Evaluate the primary endpoint of walking function after knee replacement.
